records.bootAliasReason: RM0486 Rev 2 section 9.1/Table 32 and DS14791 Rev 2 section 3.6: the ST BootROM (0x08000000) is the first code after any system reset and the boot source is an EXTERNAL device selected by BOOT0/BOOT1 pins plus OTP boot-source words (XSPI serial NOR/HyperFlash, SDMMC1/2 e.MMC, SD-card, USB or UART serial boot, or development boot). The device is ROMless, so there is no internal main flash and no fixed 0x00000000 alias; the image address is firmware/external-device defined and is not a physical device alias.
records.cacheTreatment: CACHEAXI (0x243C0000, 256 KiB, header CACHEAXI_RAM_SIZE 0x40000) is the NPU AXI cache RAM, not a user RAM bank; RM0486 Rev 2 section 10.3.1 notes it can be used at system level only when the NPU does not use its cache. It is deliberately NOT counted in ramKiB.
records.capacityReconciliation: Physical RAM counted once sums to exactly 4200 KiB. RAM banks: FLEXRAM 400 (0x24000000) + AXISRAM1 624 (0x24064000) = the 1024-KiB AXISRAM1 region; AXISRAM2 1024 (0x24100000); AXISRAM3..6 4x448 = 1792 (0x24200000-0x243BFFFF); VENCRAM 128 (0x24400000); ITCM baseline 64 (0x00000000); DTCM baseline 128 (0x20000000); AHBSRAM1/2 32 (0x28000000); BKPSRAM 8 (0x2C000000). 1024+1024+1792+128+64+128+32+8 = 4200 KiB, matching the curated catalog ramKiB 4200 and ST's '4.2-Mbyte SRAM' rounding. The ITCM/DTCM FLEXMEM extensions (up to 192 KiB ITCM + 128 KiB DTCM) are carved from the same 400-KiB FLEXRAM bank (RM0486 Rev 2 section 10.3.2 Table 35/Table 36), so FLEXRAM is counted once and the TCM extensions are not counted again; only the 64-KiB ITCM and 128-KiB DTCM baselines are separate fixed banks. CACHEAXI (256 KiB) is a cache and FSBL partitions and GFXMMU windows are not physical banks, so none is added.
records.flashReason: RM0486 Rev 2 section 3.2 and section 2.1.1 list no user/main internal flash: the Cortex-M55 boots from a 128-KiB factory mask BootROM at 0x08000000 (nonsecure) / 0x18000000 (secure) that authenticates and loads images from external memory, and the ST CMSIS header stm32n657xx.h declares no FLASH base or size. No user-programmable internal flash bank exists, so none is created.
records.fsblPartitionsExcluded: The Keil STM32N6xx_DFP memory nodes FSBL_CODE_NS (0x24180400, 0x3FC00) and FSBL_DATA_NS (0x241C0000, 0x40000) and their secure aliases are linker/bootloader partitions carved inside AXISRAM2 (0x24100000-0x241FFFFF); they are not additional physical banks and are excluded from ramKiB.
records.gfxmmuWindowsExcluded: GFXMMU virtual buffers (header GFXMMU_VIRTUAL_BUFFER0..3 at 0x25000000/0x25400000/0x25800000/0x25C00000, 4 MiB each; RM0486 Rev 2 section 2.3.2 GFXMMU SLV at 0x25000000) are virtual windows translated onto physical SRAM, not physical banks; excluded from ramKiB.
records.optionReason: RM0486 Rev 2 section 1.4 glossary: option bytes are product configuration bits stored in internal fuses (BSEC); RM0486 Rev 2 section 9.1 states boot configuration is held in BSEC BOOTROM_CONFIG OTP words. No option-byte address window exists in RM0486 Rev 2 Table 1/Table 2/Table 3, so OPTION cannot be emitted as a memory region.
records.otpReason: RM0486 Rev 2 section 4.2 and section 5 and DS14791 Rev 2 describe the OTP as internal BSEC fuses (12 Kbit effective, 376 BSEC_OTP_DATAx words) accessed only through the BSEC registers. topology.bootRomContext: ST secure BootROM (128 KiB at 0x08000000 nonsecure / 0x18000000 secure) executes on the same Cortex-M55; it is the first code after any system reset and is the root of trust, not another physical core
topology.bootSelectionMechanism: RM0486 Rev 2 section 9.1/Table 32: BOOT0 dedicated pin and the non-dedicated BOOT1 pin (or a pin selected via BSEC BOOTROM_CONFIG10/OTP_WORD19) plus the BSEC BOOTROM_CONFIG OTP words select external-flash boot, serial boot (USB/UART) or development boot

records.bitBandReason: Cortex-M0+ (ARMv6-M) does not implement the optional SRAM (0x22000000) or peripheral (0x42000000) bit-band alias regions. RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.2.2/Figure 2 and Tables 2-3 map only the SRAM/code/system/flash/OTP/option areas with no bit-band aperture, so no bit-band view is planned.
records.bootAliasReason: RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.2.2/Table 2-3 and section 2.5/Table 6: the area 0x0000 0000-0x0001 FFFF (STM32U031xx) / 0x0000 0000-0x0003 FFFF (STM32U073xx/STM32U083xx) is main flash memory, system memory or SRAM depending on the BOOT configuration. The size of the zero alias therefore tracks the selected target and is configuration dependent, so no fixed bootAliases are emitted.
records.cacheTreatment: RM0503 Rev 1 section 3.2/3.3.5: the 1-Kbyte CPU instruction cache (32 lines of 4x64 bits, ICEN) is integrated in the flash interface, not an addressable SRAM bank; no data cache is present on Cortex-M0+. No cache block is added to the RAM capacity.
records.optionReason: Option bytes are programmed through the FLASH option registers (FLASH_OPTR, FLASH_WRP1AR/WRP1BR, FLASH_SECR) which are loaded from the option-byte block during OBL; they are not an ordinary software-writable user memory region. RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.2.2/Table 2-3 and section 3.4 describe them as a product-configuration area accessed via the FLASH register interface at 0x4002 2000-0x4002 23FF, so no OPTION memory region is emitted.
records.otpReason: RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.2.2/Tables 2-3 and section 3.3.1/Table 7 define a 1-Kbyte (1024-byte, 128 double-word) user OTP area at 0x1FFF6800-0x1FFF6BFF. The ST CMSIS device header defines FLASH_OTP_BASE 0x1FFF6800 and FLASH_OTP_SIZE 0x400 (1024). OTP is one-time programmable and is not ordinary writable RAM.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: Cortex-M0+ implements no peripheral bit-band alias aperture at all; the optional Armv7-M 0x42000000 region is not present on ARMv6-M and no STM32U0 reference manual documents one. Exact peripheral registers come from the SVD provider.
records.ramAliasReason: RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.2.2 says all non-allocated areas are reserved and Table 2-3 map SRAM2 only as 0x1000 0000 (plus the 0x2000 8000 code alias); there is no evaluated 0x2000 A000-0x3FFF FFFF RAM window. The only documented same-size alternate view of a physical RAM bank is the 0x2000 8000 code-space alias of SRAM2.
sourceSections: DS14581 Rev 2 section 3.4.2 Embedded SRAM: STM32U031x4/6/8 devices have 12-Kbyte SRAM split into SRAM1 8 Kbytes at 0x2000 0000 and SRAM2 4 Kbytes at 0x1000 0000, with SRAM2 also mapped at 0x2000 8000 giving a contiguous view with SRAM1; SRAM2 is retained in Standby and write-protected with 1-Kbyte granularity
DS14581 Rev 2 features/product summary (page 1) and Table 1: 12-Kbyte SRAM and up to 64-Kbyte single-bank flash memory; the LQFP64 STM32U031R8T6 is a 64-pin part

DS14581 Rev 2 section 5 Memory mapping refers to RM0503 for the boundary addresses of all memories and peripherals

RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.3/Table 5 SRAM size per device, with the note that enabling or disabling the parity check does not change the available SRAM size, and that the 36-bit data bus costs no user SRAM

RM0503 Rev 1 section 3.4.1/Table 12-13 option bytes are a product-configuration double word set in the information block; section 3.4.2 states that after reset they are copied into FLASH_OPTR, FLASH_WRP1xR and FLASH_SECR, which are the software read/write interface, and the FLASH register block occupies 0x4002 2000-0x4002 23FF (Table 4)

RM0503 Rev 1 section 2.5/Table 6 boot modes: the BOOT0 pin, BOOT_LOCK bit and nBOOT1/BOOT_SEL/nBOOT0 option bits select main flash memory, system memory or embedded SRAM, and the selected area is aliased at 0x0000 0000 while remaining accessible at 0x0800 0000 / 0x1FFF0000 / 0x2000 0000
RM0503 Rev 1 section 3.3.5: 1-Kbyte instruction cache in the flash interface (32 lines x 4 x 64 bits), enabled by ICEN; no data cache on Cortex-M0+
CMSIS device header evidence for the U0 family: FLASH_OTP_BASE 0x1FFF6800 with FLASH_OTP_SIZE 0x400 (1024 bytes), matching RM0503 Table 7; the ST CMSIS device headers are published outside this pack

records.peripheralBitBandReason: The Cortex-M0+ core implements no bit-band alias region (Armv6-M), so neither the peripheral bit-band aperture nor any SRAM bit-band view exists.
sourceSections: RM0505 Rev 1 section 2.2.2/Table 3 (memory map and peripheral register boundary addresses): Main flash 0x1004_0000-0x100B_FFFF 512 K; SRAM0 0x2000_0000-0x2000_3FFF 16 K; SRAM1 0x2000_4000-0x2000_7FFF 16 K; SRAM2 0x2000_8000-0x2000_BFFF 16 K; SRAM3 0x2000_C000-0x2000_FFFF 16 K; OTP 0x1000_1800-0x1000_1BFF 1 K; Boot 0x0000_0000-0x0000_3FFF 16 K mirror.

RM0505 Rev 1 Figure 2 'Memory map' and section 9 'Embedded flash memory' (9.1/9.2, Table 20 'Flash memory section address'): single-bank flash, 256 pages x 2 KB, main flash 0x1004_0000-0x100B_FFFF plus User OTP 0x1000_1800-0x1000_1BFF.

DS14210 Rev 4 section 3.4.1/Table 1: on-chip nonvolatile flash 512 Kbytes and 64-Kbyte on-chip RAM split SRAM0-SRAM3 16 Kbytes each (Table 2); embedded ROM 7 KB (section 3.4.3); OTP 1 KB (section 3.4.4).

records.sramBootRule: RM Table 'Address remapping depending on the REMAP bit': after reset the Cortex-M0+ vector table is fixed at 0x0000_0000 (RM section 'Vector table'), which mirrors Main flash when FLASH_CTRL CONFIG.REMAP=0 or SRAM0 when REMAP=1. SRAM0 is otherwise always mapped at 0x2000_0000; it is never counted as a second bank.

topology.bootRomContext: ST factory UART bootloader (system memory 0x1000_0000-0x1000_17FF) runs on the same Cortex-M0+ core; not another physical core.
topology.bootSelectionMechanism: RM boot-area Table: CPU boot area 0x0000_0000-0x0000_3FFF mirrors Main flash or SRAM0 under the FLASH_CTRL CONFIG.REMAP bit; ST bootloader can additionally branch to the serial UART boot path latched on PA8-PA11/PB12-PB15 at POR (PWRC_SR2).

records.cacheTreatment: RM0473 Rev 9 section 3.3 registers flash-interface caches (1-Kbyte CPU1 ICode cache, 256-byte CPU1 DCode cache, 32-byte CPU2 S-bus cache) at the FLASH interface. They are not additional addressable SRAM banks, so no cache region is added.
records.capacityReconciliation: DS13258 Rev 9 section 2/3.3.4 state 48-Kbyte total SRAM (12 + 32 + 4), of which 36 Kbytes (SRAM2a + SRAM2b) have hardware parity. DS11929 Rev 16 section 3.3.4 uses the same three-block SRAM1/SRAM2a/SRAM2b scheme for the WB55/WB35 family. The 36-Kbyte CPU1 mirror at 0x10000000 is an alias of SRAM2a/SRAM2b, not an extra physical bank, and is modelled in aliases.
records.optionReason: RM0473 Rev 9 section 3.3.1/Table 3 maps a 128-byte option-byte block at 0x1FFF7800-0x1FFF787F; Table 9/sections 3.4.1 give the option-byte organization. The option bytes are memory mapped, not register-only.
records.otpReason: RM0473 Rev 9 section 3.3.1/Table 3 provides a 1-Kbyte (128 double word) user OTP area at 0x1FFF7000-0x1FFF73FF, one-time programmable and not ordinary writable RAM. DS13258 Rev 9 features list confirms 1 Kbyte (128 double words) OTP.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.2.3 gives a peripheral bit-band alias at 0x42000000-0x42FFFFFF, but the aperture contains reserved and device-specific holes; exact backed registers require the separate SVD/peripheral provider. No whole-aperture RAM block is planned.
sourceSections: DS13258 Rev 9 section 2 (device features: 320-Kbyte flash, 48-Kbyte SRAM of which 36 Kbytes with hardware parity) and section 3.3.4 Embedded SRAM.

DS13258 Rev 9 section 3.3.4: SRAM1 12 Kbytes at 0x20000000; SRAM2a 32 Kbytes at 0x20030000 also mirrored at 0x10000000; SRAM2b 4 Kbytes at 0x20038000 (contiguous with SRAM2a) mirrored at 0x10008000; SRAM2a and SRAM2b have hardware parity check.

DS13258 Rev 9 section 3.6 RF subsystem: a dedicated Cortex-M0+ (called CPU2) runs the real-time radio layer, confirming a dual-core die; CPU2 is modelled as a companion core, not as extra addressable SRAM.

RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.2.2/Table 1 and Figure 2: SRAM1 12 K at 0x20000000-0x20002FFF; SRAM2a 32 K at 0x20030000-0x20037FFF; SRAM2b 4 K at 0x20038000-0x20038FFF; SRAM2a/b CPU1 mirror 36 K at 0x10000000-0x10008FFF; user flash 320 K at 0x08000000-0x0804FFFF; CPU1 boot area 320 K at 0x00000000-0x0004FFFF.

RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.3/Table 2 and section 3.3.1/Table 3: boot mode selection and the information block (28-Kbyte system memory 0x1FFF0000-0x1FFF6FFF, 1-Kbyte OTP 0x1FFF7000-0x1FFF73FF, 128-byte option bytes 0x1FFF7800-0x1FFF787F).

RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.1.4 (S3 CPU2 Cortex-M0+ bus), section 2.4 CPU2 boot, and Table 1 peripheral map (IPCC 0x58000C00, HSEM 0x58001400): the STM32WB15CC has two physical CPU cores sharing SRAM and flash, with IPCC/HSEM inter-processor resources.
records.sramBootRule: RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.3: BOOT0 pin / nBOOT0 and nBOOT1 option bits select main flash, system memory or SRAM1. Boot from SRAM aliases SRAM1 (12 KiB) at 0x00000000 while SRAM1 remains at 0x20000000. SRAM2a/SRAM2b are not zero-boot targets; CPU2 (Cortex-M0+) boot is a separate option-byte reset vector (section 2.4).

topology.bootRomContext: ST factory bootloader executing on CPU1 (Cortex-M4) in system-memory boot mode; CPU2 (Cortex-M0+) is a genuine second physical core running the real-time radio layer, not a boot context.
topology.bootSelectionMechanism: RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.3/Table 2: BOOT0 pin or nBOOT0 option bit with nBOOT1 selects main flash, system memory or SRAM1 for CPU1; the zero alias is configuration dependent.
topology.secondaryBootMechanism: RM0473 Rev 9 section 2.4: after reset CPU2 boots only once CPU1 sets C2BOOT in PWR_CR4; CPU2 fetches its reset vector from flash or SRAM1/SRAM2a/SRAM2b as selected by the C2OPT/SBRV user options.

records.cacheTreatment: RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.2 registers flash-interface caches (32 cache lines, 1-Kbyte CPU1 ICode cache; eight cache lines, 256-byte CPU1 DCode cache; four cache lines, 32-byte CPU2 S-bus cache) at the FLASH interface. records.capacityReconciliation: DS11929 Rev 16 Table 2 for STM32WB55Rx gives, for the 1-Mbyte flash variant (RG), 256 Kbytes SRAM with SRAM1 192 Kbytes, matching section 3.3.4 (SRAM1 up to 192 K + SRAM2a 32 K + SRAM2b 32 K). RM0434 Rev 12 Table 1 confirms SRAM1 0x20000000-0x2002FFFF (192 K), SRAM2a 0x20030000-0x20037FFF (32 K), SRAM2b 0x20038000-0x2003FFFF (32 K). The 64-Kbyte CPU1 mirror at 0x10000000-0x1000FFFF is an alias of SRAM2a/SRAM2b, not an extra physical bank, and is modelled in aliases. The CPU2-secure sub-ranges of SRAM2a/SRAM2b are access partitions of those same single physical banks, so they add no RAM.
records.optionReason: RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.3.1/Table 3 maps a 128-byte option-byte block at 0x1FFF8000-0x1FFF807F inside the flash information block; Table 1 gives the same 0x1FFF8000-0x1FFF807F boundary. The option bytes are memory mapped, not register-only.
records.otpReason: RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.3.1/Table 3 and Table 1 provide a 1-Kbyte (128 double word) user OTP area at 0x1FFF7000-0x1FFF73FF, one-time programmable and not ordinary writable RAM. It is distinct from the main flash and from the option bytes.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.2.3 gives a CPU1 peripheral bit-band alias at 0x42000000-0x42FFFFFF, but the aperture contains reserved and device-specific holes; exact backed registers require the separate SVD/peripheral provider. No whole-aperture RAM block is planned.
records.sharedMemoryNotes: RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.4.1 (SBRSA/SNBRSA) and DS11929 Rev 16 section 3.3.4: SRAM2a/SRAM2b are owned by CPU2, and a user-option-selected section is CPU2-secure and cannot be accessed by CPU1. CPU1 only reaches the non-secure section through the 0x10000000 mirror. Because the secure section boundary is option-byte configuration-dependent, CPU2 is modelled as the writer of SRAM2A/SRAM2B and CPU1 is not granted write access, rather than overclaiming shared read/write.
sourceSections: DS11929 Rev 16 section 2 description: hosts an Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU (CPU1, application) and a dedicated Arm Cortex-M0+ (CPU2, real-time low-layer radio) on one die; IPCC with six bidirectional channels and HSEM hardware semaphores share common resources between the two processors.

DS11929 Rev 16 section 3.3.3 Embedded flash memory and Table 2 devices features: STM32WB55Rx RG = 1 Mbyte flash and 256 Kbytes SRAM (SRAM1 192 Kbytes); the flash is shared between CPU1 and CPU2 on a time-sharing basis with a CPU2-secured section.
DS11929 Rev 16 section 3.5 Boot modes: BOOT0 pin and BOOT1 option bit select user flash, system memory or embedded SRAM; the devices always boot on CPU1.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.2.2/Table 1: SRAM2b 0x20038000-0x2003FFFF 32 K on AHB4; SRAM2a 0x20030000-0x20037FFF 32 K on AHB4; SRAM1 0x20000000-0x2002FFFF 192 K on AHB1; flash options 0x1FFF8000-0x1FFF807F 128 B; OTP 0x1FFF7000-0x1FFF73FF 1 K; boot loader 0x1FFF0000-0x1FFF6FFF 28 K; SRAM2a/b CPU1 mirror 0x10000000-0x1000FFFF 64 K; user flash 0x08000000-0x080FFFFF 1 M; CPUn boot area 0x00000000-0x000FFFFF 1 M.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.3.1/Table 3 flash single-bank organization: 256 pages of 4 Kbytes at 0x08000000-0x080FFFFF; information block system memory 0x1FFF0000-0x1FFF6FFF 28 K, OTP 0x1FFF7000-0x1FFF73FF 1 K, option bytes 0x1FFF8000-0x1FFF807F 128 B.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.2.3 Bit banding: the CPU1 map has an SRAM bit-band alias 0x22000000-0x227FFFFF and a peripheral bit-band alias 0x42000000-0x42FFFFFF; SRAM1, SRAM2a and SRAM2b are mapped to the bit-band region and bit-band is available only to CPU1 accesses.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.3/Table 2 boot modes and section 2.4 CPU2 boot: main flash, system memory or SRAM1 selection for CPU1; CPU2 boots only after CPU1 sets C2BOOT in PWR_CR4 and may boot from anywhere in user flash or SRAM1/SRAM2a/SRAM2b.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.2.2/Table 1 and sections 37 (IPCC) and 38 (HSEM): IPCC register block 0x58000C00-0x58000FFF with twelve channels (six per direction) and HSEM register block 0x58001400-0x580017FF providing hardware semaphores between CPU1 and CPU2.

RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.10.18/FLASH secure-area option bytes (BRSD/SBRSA for SRAM2a, NBRSD/SNBRSA for SRAM2b): a section of SRAM2a and SRAM2b with 1-Kbyte granularity can be made CPU2-secure so CPU1 reads return no data; the banks remain single physical banks.
RM0434 Rev 12 section 3.4.1 secure SRAM2 option bytes (BRSD/NBRSD, SBRSA/SNBRSA) and section 2.4 CPU2 boot: a configuration-dependent section of SRAM2a/SRAM2b is CPU2-secure and inaccessible to CPU1.
records.sramBootRule: RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.3/Table 2: BOOT0 pin and nBOOT1/nBOOT0 option bits select main flash, system memory or SRAM1. CPU2 boots only after CPU1 sets C2BOOT in PWR_CR4 and fetches its own reset vector from user flash or SRAM1/SRAM2a/SRAM2b (section 2.4).

topology.bootRomContext: ST factory bootloader executing on CPU1 (Cortex-M4) in system-memory boot mode; CPU2 (Cortex-M0+) holds the radio network stack in a flash region secured to the RF subsystem. CPU2 is a genuine physical core, not a boot context.
topology.bootSelectionMechanism: RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.3/Table 2: BOOT0 pin or nBOOT0 option bit with nBOOT1 selects main flash, system memory or SRAM1 for CPU1; the zero alias is configuration dependent.
topology.secondaryBootMechanism: RM0434 Rev 12 section 2.4: after reset CPU2 boots only once CPU1 sets C2BOOT in PWR_CR4; CPU2 fetches its reset vector from user flash or SRAM1/SRAM2a/SRAM2b as selected by the C2OPT and SBRV user options.

records.bitBandReason: The Cortex-M33 (Armv8-M) does not implement the optional SRAM or peripheral bit-band alias regions. No STM32WBA reference manual documents a 0x22000000/0x42000000 bit-band aperture, and the Cortex-M33 does not expose the 32x word-aliasing hardware, so no bit-band view is emitted for any of the physical RAM banks.
records.bootAliasReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 4/Table 21 and Table 22: the BOOT0 pin or NBOOT0 option bit plus NSWBOOT0, the NSBOOTADDx/SECBOOTADD0 option-byte fields and TZEN select the boot entry address (non-secure default 0x08000000 user flash, non-secure alternative 0x0BF88000 bootloader, secure default 0x0C000000 user flash, or RSS 0x0FF80000). RM0493 Rev 2 Figure 3/Table 4 reserve 0x00000000-0x07FFFFFF, so no fixed zero-address boot alias is imposed and bootAliases is empty; the mapping is configuration dependent. Embedded-SRAM boot is one of the selectable boot memories (any address in embedded SRAM) but it too is set by the boot-address option bytes rather than by a hardware zero alias.
records.cacheTreatment: The 8-Kbyte two-way ICACHE (RM0493 Rev 2 section 8.3/Table 66) is a flash/SRAM interface cache, not an addressable RAM bank, so no cache block is added to ramKiB. The ICACHE remap regions (RM0493 Rev 2 section 8.4.7) only remap code alias addresses onto existing SRAM, so they add no memory either.

disputedFacts.conflict: RM0493 Rev 2 section 2.3.3 states SRAM1 is 64 Kbytes on STM32WBA5xGx and 32 Kbytes on STM32WBA5xEx, which would give a 512-Kbyte device only 32 Kbytes of SRAM1 (64 KiB total with SRAM2). RM0493 Rev 2 table 1 device-dependent note 2 also gives 32-Kbyte SRAM1 / 512-Kbyte user flash for STM32WBA5xEx.
disputedFacts.fact: SRAM1 capacity on STM32WBA25CEU7 (512-Kbyte flash, STM32WBA5xEx sales type)
disputedFacts.preferredSource: CMSIS header stm32wba25xx.h plus the repository T033 oracle for STM32WBA25CEU7
disputedFacts.resolution: Header SRAM1_SIZE 0x10000 (64 Kbytes) and SRAM2_SIZE 0x8000 (32 Kbytes) are used, matching the committed oracle ramKiB 96 with initial SP 0x20010000; RM0493 Rev 2 never names the STM32WBA25xx and its WBA52xx-only scope is the reason the RM reading is not adopted.

records.optionReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 7.3.1 states the option bytes are not mapped to any memory address and can be accessed only through the flash register interface; section 7.4.1/Table 44 maps the user option bytes onto the FLASH_OPTR/SECWMRx/NSBOOTADDx/SECBOOTADD0 registers and section 7.4.2 gives the OPTKEYR/OPTSTRT programming sequence. DS14127 Rev 2 Table 3/Table 4 note the same. No addressable option-byte region is emitted.
records.otpReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 7.3.1/Table 39 provides a 512-byte OTP area (up to 32 quad-words) at 0x0BF90000-0x0BF901FF on STM32WBA5xGx devices, one-time programmable, written only through non-secure access and readable by secure and non-secure access. DS14127 Rev 2 section 3.5 confirms a 512-byte OTP for the STM32WBA52xx. The header gives FLASH_OTP_BASE = SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS + offset and FLASH_OTP_SIZE 0x200. On STM32WBA65xx the header places SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS at 0x0BF90000 and FLASH_OTP_BASE at +0x10000, so the OTP is emitted at 0x0BFA0000-0x0BFA01FF. This 512-byte user OTP is not ordinary writable RAM.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: Cortex-M33 implements no peripheral bit-band alias aperture; the optional Armv7-M 0x42000000 peripheral bit-band region was removed in Armv8-M, and no STM32WBA reference manual documents one.
sourceSections: RM0493 Rev 2 section 2.3.2/Table 4 (memory map and peripheral register boundary addresses): user flash non-secure 0x08000000, secure 0x0C000000; SRAM1 NS 0x20000000 / S 0x30000000; SRAM2 NS 0x20010000 / S 0x30010000; RSS-Boot 0x0BF80000-0x0BF85FFF, RSS-Lib 0x0BF86000-0x0BF87FFF, Bootloader 0x0BF88000-0x0BF8FFFF, OTP 0x0BF90000-0x0BF901FF, Engineering bytes 0x0BF90500-0x0BF93FFF, user options 0x0BF94000-0x0BF97FFF; RXTXRAM 0x48028000-0x4802BFFF, SEQRAM 0x48021000-0x480211FF

RM0493 Rev 2 section 8.3/Table 66 and section 8.4.7 Address remapping: 8-Kbyte two-way ICACHE plus a software-configurable 2-Mbyte-granularity remap of up to four SRAM regions into a code alias address; no fixed SRAM code alias exists
RM0493 Rev 2 section 3.5.1/Table 1 (TrustZone supported): option-byte TZEN activates Armv8-M TrustZone secure/non-secure worlds

CMSIS header stm32wba25xx.h (STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-wba @3373b40fa3b71ce114f58b170acd0f8833d42508, sha256 0f58c92548df65e395a55e970497094aa09900dbbec23e906cfebab712ea1317) gives FLASH_BASE_NS 0x08000000, SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS 0x0BF88000, SRAM1_BASE_NS 0x20000000 / SRAM1_SIZE 0x10000, SRAM2_BASE_NS 0x20010000 / SRAM2_SIZE 0x10000, SRAM6_BASE_NS 0x48028000 / SRAM6_SIZE 0x4000 (2.4 GHz RADIO TXRX SRAM), SEQSRAM_BASE_NS 0x48021000 / SEQSRAM_SIZE 0x200, FLASH_OTP_BASE SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS+0x8000, FLASH_OTP_SIZE 0x200

The RM0493 Rev 2 title page and introduction cover only the STM32WBA52xx; the STM32WBA25xx memory quantities are taken from the CMSIS header stm32wba25xx.h (FLASH_SIZE default 0x80000 = 512 Kbytes, SRAM1_SIZE 0x10000 = 64 Kbytes, SRAM2_SIZE 0x8000 = 32 Kbytes, SRAM6_SIZE 0x2800 = 10 Kbytes RXTXRAM). The repository T033 oracle/oracle manifest for STM32WBA25CEU7 (src/test/resources/oracles/stm32-core-samples/STM32WBA25CEU7.json) records ramKiB 96 from facts FLASH_BASE_NS, SRAM1_BASE_NS and SRAM1_SIZE with initial SP 0x20010000, i.e. an end-of-SRAM1 stack; RM0493 Rev 2 section 2.3.3 reads 'SRAM1 up to 64-Kbyte (sales type STM32WBA5xGx 64-Kbyte, STM32WBA5xEx 32-Kbyte)' which would give 32 Kbytes for a 512-Kbyte WBA25. The header values (64+32=96 Kbytes) are used and the RM reading is recorded as contested.

records.bitBandReason: The Cortex-M33 (Armv8-M) does not implement the optional SRAM or peripheral bit-band alias regions. No STM32WBA reference manual documents a 0x22000000/0x42000000 bit-band aperture, and the Cortex-M33 does not expose the 32x word-aliasing hardware, so no bit-band view is emitted for any of the physical RAM banks.
records.bootAliasReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 4/Table 21 and Table 22: the BOOT0 pin or NBOOT0 option bit plus NSWBOOT0, the NSBOOTADDx/SECBOOTADD0 option-byte fields and TZEN select the boot entry address (non-secure default 0x08000000 user flash, non-secure alternative 0x0BF88000 bootloader, secure default 0x0C000000 user flash, or RSS 0x0FF80000). RM0493 Rev 2 Figure 3/Table 4 reserve 0x00000000-0x07FFFFFF, so no fixed zero-address boot alias is imposed and bootAliases is empty; the mapping is configuration dependent. Embedded-SRAM boot is one of the selectable boot memories (any address in embedded SRAM) but it too is set by the boot-address option bytes rather than by a hardware zero alias.
records.cacheTreatment: The 8-Kbyte two-way ICACHE (RM0493 Rev 2 section 8.3/Table 66) is a flash/SRAM interface cache, not an addressable RAM bank, so no cache block is added to ramKiB. The ICACHE remap regions (RM0493 Rev 2 section 8.4.7) only remap code alias addresses onto existing SRAM, so they add no memory either.
records.optionReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 7.3.1 states the option bytes are not mapped to any memory address and can be accessed only through the flash register interface; section 7.4.1/Table 44 maps the user option bytes onto the FLASH_OPTR/SECWMRx/NSBOOTADDx/SECBOOTADD0 registers and section 7.4.2 gives the OPTKEYR/OPTSTRT programming sequence. DS14127 Rev 2 Table 3/Table 4 note the same. No addressable option-byte region is emitted.
records.otpReason: RM0493 Rev 2 section 7.3.1/Table 39 provides a 512-byte OTP area (up to 32 quad-words) at 0x0BF90000-0x0BF901FF on STM32WBA5xGx devices, one-time programmable, written only through non-secure access and readable by secure and non-secure access. DS14127 Rev 2 section 3.5 confirms a 512-byte OTP for the STM32WBA52xx. The header gives FLASH_OTP_BASE = SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS + offset and FLASH_OTP_SIZE 0x200. On STM32WBA65xx the header places SYSTEM_FLASH_BASE_NS at 0x0BF90000 and FLASH_OTP_BASE at +0x10000, so the OTP is emitted at 0x0BFA0000-0x0BFA01FF. This 512-byte user OTP is not ordinary writable RAM.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: Cortex-M33 implements no peripheral bit-band alias aperture; the optional Armv7-M 0x42000000 peripheral bit-band region was removed in Armv8-M, and no STM32WBA reference manual documents one.

records.bitBandReason: Cortex-M0+ (ARMv6-M) implements no optional SRAM (0x2200_0000) or peripheral (0x4200_0000) bit-band alias aperture. RM0511 Rev 5 section 2.3 and Figure 2/Table 3 map only SRAM, main flash, system memory, OTP and peripherals with no bit-band region, so no bit-band view is planned.
records.bootAliasReason: RM0511 Rev 5 section 2.3.1/Table 5-6: the 0x0000_0000-0x0003_FFFF CPU boot area is a mirror of main flash memory or SRAM0 depending on the REMAP bit in the flash controller CONFIG register. Only two of the three possible zero-based targets exist (main flash and SRAM0); system memory is not remappable at 0x0000_0000, so no fixed bootAliases are emitted.
records.cacheTreatment: RM0511 Rev 5 section 9.2 and DS14221 Rev 4 section 3.3.1 describe a single main flash memory with a flash interface but no addressable instruction/data cache bank; no cache block is added to the RAM capacity.
records.optionReason: RM0511 Rev 5 section 2.2.2/Table 3 and Figure 2 list no user option-byte memory region: the only option mechanism is a flash-controller page-write-protection register set (section 9.4 PAGEPROT0/PAGEPROT1) plus a configuration register (section 9.3.2) with the REMAP bit, and an 'Option-byte loader hardware mechanism reserved for ST analog trimming bits' (section 9.2). There is no 0x1FFF... option block, so no OPTION memory region is emitted.
records.otpReason: RM0511 Rev 5 Table 21 (Flash memory section address, page 201) and section 9.2 define a 1-Kbyte user OTP area at 0x1000_1800-0x1000_1BFF managed by the flash controller, programmed once and not ordinary writable RAM. DS14221 Rev 4 section 3.3.3 confirms the 1-Kbyte one-time-programmable user data memory.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: The ARMv6-M Cortex-M0+ implements no peripheral bit-band alias region at all; RM0511 Rev 5 Table 3 maps APB0/APB1/AHB0/AHB-RF peripherals directly with no 0x4200_0000 aperture. Exact peripheral registers come from the SVD provider.
sourceSections: DS14221 Rev 4 section 8/Table 73 Ordering information scheme: STM32 WL 33 K C V 6 TR, pin count C = 48, memory configuration C = 256-Kbyte flash / 32-Kbyte RAM, V = VFQFPN, 6 = -40 to +85 C, TR = tape and reel, so STM32WL33CCV6TR is the 256-KiB flash / 32-KiB SRAM 48-pin VFQFPN part

DS14221 Rev 4 features (page 1) and section 3.3.1/3.3.2: 64/128/256-Kbyte flash, 16/32-Kbyte SRAM; STM32WL33xx integrates 32 Kbytes of SRAM split into two 16-Kbyte banks (SRAM0 always supplied, SRAM1 switchable), one flash bank of 256 Kbytes with 2-Kbyte pages
DS14221 Rev 4 section 3.3.3: 1-Kbyte one-time-programmable (OTP) user data memory, frozen by writing the last word at 0x1000_1BFC
DS14221 Rev 4 section 3.1: single Cortex-M0+ core with radio subsystem, one flash memory, two SRAM banks

RM0511 Rev 5 section 2.2.2/Table 3 and Figure 2 memory map: main flash 0x1004_0000-0x1007_FFFF (up to 256 Kbytes), SRAM0 0x2000_0000-0x2000_3FFF (16 Kbytes, first 48 bytes 0x2000_0000-0x2000_002F reserved per Table 4, user RAM from 0x2000_0030), SRAM1 0x2000_4000-0x2000_7FFF (16 Kbytes, STM32WL33xx only), OTP 0x1000_1800-0x1000_1BFF (1 Kbyte), boot mirror 0x0000_0000-0x0003_FFFF

records.optionReason: RM0551 provides flash page protection and the CONFIG.REMAP bit through the FLASH controller registers; no addressable option-byte memory region is defined.
records.otpReason: RM0551 table 21 defines a 1-KiB user OTP area at 0x10001800-0x10001BFF, writable once through the OTPWRITE command.
records.peripheralBitBandReason: Cortex-M0+ implements no peripheral bit-band alias aperture; exact backed registers require the SVD provider.
